w: Ten and a half miles of petrified sand dunes and the eroded remains of ancient sea beds, a few miles northeast of town - the Slickrock Trail put Moab on the mountain-biking map. Riders rate it among the area's toughest routes, testing both technique and lungs across the sandstone.
s: Petrified dunes that put Moab on the biking map
_facts: 10.5-mile mountain bike trail in Grand County, near Moab
Crosses petrified sand dunes and eroded ancient sea beds
Rated one of the more technically and physically demanding rides in the area

w: On a sheltered sandstone wall at the mouth of Courthouse Wash, just inside Arches National Park, a series of large pictographs built up layer upon layer over a long span of time. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, the panel records the people who moved through this canyon long before the park existed.
s: Rock art layered over centuries at a canyon mouth
_facts: Large pictograph panel at the mouth of Courthouse Wash
Located in Arches National Park, just north of Moab
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places

w: A 260-foot spire of Entrada sandstone above the Park Avenue Trail, Argon Tower's summit rises 450 vertical feet in just 400 feet of horizontal distance - a near-sheer wall of rock. Its runoff reaches the Colorado River, and it appears in the 1989 opening credits of Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade.
s: A sandstone spire that opened Indiana Jones in 1989
_facts: 4,750-foot pillar of Entrada Sandstone in Arches National Park, 260 feet tall
Summit rises 450 vertical feet over 400 horizontal feet above Park Avenue Trail
Drains to the Colorado River via Courthouse Wash
Appeared in the 1989 opening credits of Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
